title: Restricted Soil-Temperature Transactional Runtime Composition Architecture-Invariant Audit

interpretation.DIRECTLY_QUALIFIED: The invariant is materially exercised by F-MR39 source and qualification evidence.
interpretation.PRESERVED_BY_SCOPE_LOCK: F-MR39 does not modify the governing seam and the bounded/source-blob locks provide evidence that no conflicting dependency was introduced.
interpretation.AUDITED_NONCLAIM: The invariant was reviewed, but the corresponding broader capability is deliberately not qualified by F-MR39. The nonclaim is retained explicitly.

invariants.evidence: Soil temperature is composed into the existing kernel/runtime path; no second kernel or use-case-specific SWAP kernel is introduced.
Only bounded runtime modules change. No file, parser, path, file unit or legacy-I/O dependency is added to kernel or process code.
Thermal parameters, forcing, committed state, numerical configuration/workspace and observations remain distinct typed categories in the serialized runtime backend.
soil_temperature is an allocatable substate of the committed physical state and is absent for inactive columns; mixed enabled/disabled qualification verifies compact optional state.
soil_temperature_workspace is owned by the backend model/worker and is absent from committed state and parameter carriers; the static gate checks this explicitly.
Optional thermal state does not force allocation on inactive logical columns; mixed MultiSWAP isolation passes. No parallel-throughput or vector-layout performance claim is made.
Richards and thermal updates execute inside one outer candidate transaction. Injected thermal failure leaves revision, time and full committed-state fingerprint unchanged.
After a rejected thermal trial, rerun with corrected forcing is fingerprint-identical to a fresh run from the same committed origin, qualifying exact retry origin semantics.
The runtime passes generic numeric t0,t1 to the thermal process; qualification uses non-calendar-aligned fractional times and introduces no day/month/year boundary.
No coupling-window code or fixed 00:00 boundary is introduced; generic interval semantics are preserved.
Kernel transaction and coupling architecture are blob-locked/unmodified; F-MR39 composes only a process into the existing transaction path.
No groundwater interface contract, head/flux sign convention or groundwater residual handling is changed.
Enabled runs retain hard water-mass closure; thermal energy is not added to water storage/mass. The gate verifies water mass and the storage routine excludes soil_temperature.
No groundwater-interface sensitivity API or Jacobian/factorisation path is changed by this runtime-composition workunit.

The composed path performs the existing Richards solve once and then a local restricted thermal update; no additional full-column water solve is introduced. Coupling production-cost qualification itself is out of scope.
A mixed enabled/disabled serialized MultiSWAP population is exercised and each column matches its isolated reference endpoint. Parallel throughput/scaling remains an explicit nonclaim.
No MODFLOW-cell/tile mapping or one-to-one groundwater-cell assumption is added to SWAP state or process code.
No deep-vadose transfer-zone functionality is moved into SWAP or altered.
No deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition logic or associated storage accounting is changed.
The soil-water solver contract and qualified hydraulic-view seam are blob-locked. Thermal composition consumes semantic hydraulic views and does not bind the process to Richards internals.
The F-VQ58 restricted soil-temperature process is reused byte-for-byte and replayed from its exact scientific authority; no duplicate or rewritten thermal physics is introduced.
Thermal physics receives process_hydraulic_view_t start/end views. The hydraulic-view, kernel and transaction seam blobs are locked, and no HeadCalc internals are imported by the thermal composition.
soil_temperature_active is a physical configuration choice; numerical configuration/workspace remains separate and no scientific tolerance is relaxed.
F-MR39 does not qualify thermal-active throughput, bounded-cost fallback or batch wall-time predictability. It adds no extra full Richards solve, but performance qualification is explicitly deferred.
The serialized reference backend remains the qualification path and exact F-VQ58 scientific authority is replayed in O0/O2.
Runtime observation exposes thermal active/executed/status plus energy-accounting diagnostics while existing water solver diagnostics remain available.
Inactive columns have no thermal physical-state allocation; persistent thermal state appears only when active, while scratch is backend/worker-local.

Composition occurs in runtime/backend. The qualified thermal process receives local state/forcing/views and is not given MODFLOW tile fractions, transfer-zone relationships or system-composition knowledge.
No midnight/day-run, .swp-file, MODFLOW-attachment or direct solver-internal assumption is introduced; time is generic and process dependencies are explicit typed inputs/views.
This artifact records an explicit per-invariant audit for the F-MR39 architecture change and distinguishes directly qualified behavior from preserved seams and bounded nonclaims.

bounded_nonclaims: no thermal-active parallel-throughput or scaling qualification
no bounded-cost fallback qualification for difficult thermal columns
no frost or latent-heat phase-change physics
no new soil-temperature science or tolerance policy
